analysis.title: AI Value Chain: How much does a GW of AI ASIC data center capacity actually cost?
key_insights: Bernstein extends its Nvidia Blackwell and Vera Rubin pod-level economics work to AMD and ASIC architectures, based on expert conversations, supply chain checks and third-party data.

Vera Rubin NVL72 rack estimate cut to $7.5M from $9.1M. Drivers: lower per-rack NAND content, more conservative HBM4 pricing ($30.6/GB vs $48/GB), revised networking, cooling and power delivery content from Asia channel checks, and latest DRAM and NAND prices. The new figure is in line with supply chain expectations of $7-8M per rack.

AMD MI455X Helios rack estimated at $7.3M, similar to Vera Rubin. AMD earns lower GPU margins so compute content is lower, despite higher CPU value than Nvidia's Vera. Networking content is much higher because AMD includes up to 3 NICs per GPU.

OpenAI Jalapeno estimated at $5.0M per pod (the detailed text says $4.9M). The design differs sharply from Nvidia's: a larger scale-up domain, data held locally in HBM and DRAM, and less reliance on scale-out and NAND. OpenAI's disclosures are less complete than Nvidia's or AMD's, but the estimates are consistent with OpenAI's stated design goals.

Google TPU v7 Ironwood estimated at $2.7M per rack. Bernstein has low conviction in the granular estimates because disclosures are lacking and expects significant revisions as Google discloses more with external sales. TPU v8 details are awaited.

Total data center capex per GW ranges from $34.6B (Jalapeno) to $39.5B (Vera Rubin NVL72). Other estimates: GB200 NVL72 $36.5B, MI455X $35.7B, TPU v7 $39.0B. Out-of-rack cost is $12.0-12.7B per GW, near the low end of the prior $12-15B range.

Operating costs are small next to capex. Electricity at $0.15/kWh is about $1.3B per GW per year, while Rubin depreciation on a 6-year cycle is about $6.6B a year. Hourly economics are therefore weighted toward servers, storage and networking.
Utilization-adjusted hourly cost per GPU (40% utilization, 5-year life): H100 $0.53, GB200 $1.77, VR NVL72 $3.18, MI455X $3.23, TPU v7 $1.29, Jalapeno $1.27.

Estimated AI accelerator rack shipments imply 36 GW in 2026 and 43 GW in 2027, well above Bernstein's US capacity adds of 18 GW in 2026E and 26 GW in 2027E. Bernstein attributes the gap to timing and to growing international builds amid US data center delays, such as OpenAI's Firmus deal across Australia, Singapore, Indonesia and Malaysia.
Bernstein sees accelerating available compute, helped by the Rubin cycle and wider ASIC adoption, as an unlock for further AI adoption. End-user adoption appears to have accelerated in 2026.

Vera Rubin memory and storage content is about $1.8M per rack: HBM $697K (20.7 TB at $30.6/GB with a 10% Nvidia markup), CPU DRAM $888K (54 TB at $16.45/GB, up from $14.85/GB), NAND $222K (576 TB at $0.38/GB, up from $0.37/GB). Memory prices remain volatile and estimates go stale quickly.

Vera Rubin networking content is about $1.2M per rack: roughly $600K scale-up, $500K scale-out and $80K front-end. Power content is $102K (20% of racks with a sidecar at $150K, the rest near $90K). Cooling is $102K, double Blackwell's $51K. Chassis is about $100K.

The AMD MI455X Helios rack estimate uses max-spec assumptions for NAND and CPU DRAM, which Bernstein says may be aggressive. Benchmarking NAND to 8 GB per GPU like Nvidia would give $2.4M of memory and storage per rack instead of $2.7M.

Jalapeno uses an OCS layer in place of normal scale-out switches, with about $300K of Broadcom Tomahawk 6 scale-up switch content and only $109K of transceivers. TPU v7 uses MEMS OCS for scale-up (about $154K per rack), a Lumentum-type solution rumored at $600 per port.

sector_views.sector: AI data center hardware and infrastructure
sector_views.rationale: Rack content, GW shipments (36 GW in 2026E, 43 GW in 2027E) and capex per GW of roughly $35-40B point to large spending. Most covered names are rated Outperform.

risk_factors: DRAM and NAND price volatility can make the rack estimates stale quickly.
Disclosures for Google TPU v7 and OpenAI Jalapeno are limited, so granular estimates may need significant revision.
The AMD Helios and Jalapeno NAND estimates use max-spec assumptions that may be aggressive and carry downside to implied NAND demand.
Nvidia is expected to give a more conservative HBM spec for Rubin Ultra.
US data center delays may lower the share of capacity deployed in the US.
geopolitical: US data center delays from operational, power availability and policy constraints are pushing AI labs toward non-US partners, such as OpenAI's deal with Firmus across Australia, Singapore, Indonesia and Malaysia.

theme_stances.key_argument: Capex per GW of about $35-40B across Nvidia, AMD and ASIC architectures, with growing compute availability helping AI adoption.
